answer: Ferrous resource ledger. Each new agent identity must claim a unique compute slot from a shared vine of hardware-attested capacity; slots are non-transferable and only issue after a fresh physical enclave measurement. A clone therefore costs a full hardware procurement plus attestation overhead, while a legitimate agent pays only an incremental slot. At the annual summit, unused slots are reclaimed, so mass-registering clones yields idle sunk hardware that cannot be resold or repurposed.
